content: 1. Inform your doctor and pharmacist about all the products you are using, including prescription drugs, over-the-counter medications, and herbal supplements. 2. Notify your doctor if you have received a nasal flu vaccine within two weeks prior to starting treatment with this medication, as it may reduce the effectiveness of the nasal flu vaccine. 3. In the event of an overdose, if the individual exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call emergency services (911) immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. 4. This medication is not a replacement for the flu vaccine. 5. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is close to the time of your next dose (within two hours), skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. 6. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. 7. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. 8. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information tailored to your specific health needs. 9. Oseltamivir, commonly known by the brand name Tamiflu, is used to treat symptoms caused by the influenza virus (flu). It may also be used to prevent the flu if you have been exposed to someone with the flu, such as a sick household member, or during a community flu outbreak. 10. This medication works by inhibiting the growth of the flu virus. However, it is not a substitute for the flu vaccine. 11. Before starting this medication, read the patient information leaflet provided by your pharmacist. 12. Take this medication orally, with or without food. If stomach upset occurs, taking it with food or milk may help. 13. Begin taking this medication as soon as flu symptoms appear or as soon as possible after exposure to the flu virus. 14. To prevent the flu, take oseltamivir as directed by your doctor, usually once daily for at least 10 days. 15. The dosage is determined based on your medical condition and response to treatment. 16. If you are unable to swallow capsules, consult your doctor or pharmacist about the liquid suspension form of oseltamivir. If the liquid form is unavailable, you may open the capsule and mix its contents with a small amount of sweetened liquid (e.g., regular or sugar-free chocolate syrup, corn syrup, caramel topping, or light brown sugar dissolved in water) as directed by your doctor or pharmacist. 17. For optimal effectiveness, take this medication at evenly spaced intervals. 18. To help you remember, take it at the same time(s) every day. 19. Continue taking this medication for the full prescribed duration, even if symptoms improve after a few days. 20. Common side effects include nausea and vomiting. 21. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. 22. Rarely, the flu itself or oseltamivir may cause serious mental or mood changes, which are more likely in children. 23. Severe allergic reactions to this medication are rare. 24. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. 25. Before taking oseltamivir, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. 26. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed. 27. Oseltamivir passes into breast milk but is unlikely to harm a nursing infant. 28. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. 29. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. 30. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. 31. Notify your doctor if you have received a nasal flu vaccine within two weeks before starting this medication, as it may reduce the vaccine's effectiveness. 32. In case of overdose, if severe symptoms such as passing out or trouble breathing occur, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. 33. This medication is not a substitute for the flu vaccine. 34. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is close to the time of your next dose (within two hours), skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. 35. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. 36. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. 37. This information was last revised in August 2024.
